terms.definition: Contains chemicals that react to produce electricity; the voltage depends on the electrodes and the electrolyte.
terms.examiner: Separate Chemistry. The bigger the difference in reactivity, the bigger the voltage.

terms.definition: Two or more cells connected in series to give a greater voltage.
Stops producing electricity when a reactant is used up, as in an alkaline battery.
terms.examiner: Separate Chemistry. Rechargeable cells reverse the reaction when an external current is supplied.

terms.definition: A cell supplied with a fuel and oxygen (from air) that oxidises the fuel electrochemically to produce a potential difference.
terms.examiner: Separate Chemistry. Hydrogen fuel cells only produce water.

terms.definition: At the anode H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻; at the cathode O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O.
